A reviewer claims this security issue:
  title: SQL Injection via string concatenation
  lines: 2-2 (new file)
  rationale: The `name` parameter is interpolated directly into a raw SQL string without sanitization or parameterization. An attacker controlling `name` can break out of the string literal (e.g. `' OR '1'='1`) to manipulate query logic, dump arbitrary data, or—depending on the DB driver—execute stacked statements. The sink is `this.db.raw(...)` which executes the constructed string verbatim.

The ONLY context you may use is this hunk:

Lines show NEW-file line numbers; + added, - removed, space unchanged.

   2 +   find(name) { return this.db.raw("SELECT * FROM t WHERE name = '" + name + "'"); }

Is the finding real and supported by THIS hunk? Try to refute it before agreeing. Report your outcome (upheld/refuted), your confidence, and your reasoning.
